storyboard.claim: Darrow refuses to cower when Dan humiliates him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dan flicks a pebble toward Darrow's head; Darrow stands his ground in the mine tunnel.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the Gold section on the Red's defiance in the mines.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Darrow's pride before any Gold appears, so the later shame reads as a change.

storyboard.claim: Darrow answers the armed guard with a sarcastic, insubordinate bow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow bows low and sweeping to Dan, who stands armed with his hand on his weapon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the pebble moment with Darrow's answer.
storyboard.addedInformation: Smirk gives the bow a sarcastic edge rather than submission.

storyboard.claim: Darrow knows Dan could beat him but holds him in contempt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow's hard contemptuous stare at the mine guard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the bow: contempt, not fear.
storyboard.addedInformation: Separates fear of the guard's strength from disrespect for the man.

storyboard.claim: Darrow is crushed the moment the Gold heir arrives.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow sags on the red Mars horizon as a tall gold-clad Gold steps off the ship.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pride of 202 collapses at the arrival of the Gold.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: Nero is not in the story bible; titus stands in as the arriving Gold figure and the callout names Nero.

callout.text: I scarcely want to look at him

storyboard.claim: Darrow admits shame and cannot look at the Gold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow turns his head away and down, eyes averted from an unseen Gold.
storyboard.onScreenText: I scarcely want to look at him
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the shame that follows the Gold's arrival.
storyboard.addedInformation: The averted gaze is the shame; the callout gives his own words.

storyboard.claim: Darrow feels his red body soils the Gold finery.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow, dusty and small, stands on the marble floor of the gold hall, apart from the gilded space.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves the shame into the Gold hall itself.
storyboard.addedInformation: The marble and gold of the hall do the work; Darrow is visibly out of place.

storyboard.claim: The visual majesty of the Gold hierarchy overrides the Red's rebellion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A gold laurel trophy at the centre of the gold hall; Darrow small beneath it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the shame works: the majesty of rank.
storyboard.addedInformation: The laurel reads as status and rank, the power being admired.

storyboard.claim: Lower colors police their own self-worth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow looks down at his own dusty hands, judging himself against the gold hall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalises Darrow's shame to every lower colour.
storyboard.addedInformation: Self-judgment is shown through the lowered look, not a mirror, which would read as appearance.

storyboard.claim: If you feel dirty before your ruler, you will never try to overthrow them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains read as bound: Darrow stands between the chains beside the proud Gold.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The consequence of 207: self-policing becomes a cage.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains show the bond the viewer cannot otherwise see, the cage the narration calls physical.

callout.text: The physical narrative is the cage

storyboard.claim: The gold world's physical presentation is itself the cage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow walks through the gilded hall, hemmed in by tall marble columns.
storyboard.onScreenText: The physical narrative is the cage
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the mechanism of 200-208: beauty as confinement.
storyboard.addedInformation: The walk through columns shows the enclosure; the callout names it.

storyboard.claim: The Golds cannot be soft; they must be the monsters they project.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus stands in the gold hall with a hard, threatening face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The cage needs cruel rulers to keep it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Angry face reads threat, not warmth, so the monster claim is visible.

storyboard.claim: The Golds justify ruling through absolute cruelty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus speaks with a sinister, self-assured smirk in the gold hall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Raises the question the narrator then answers with the passage.
storyboard.addedInformation: Smirk reads cruel charm, not a friendly man.

storyboard.claim: Darrow is surgically carved to pass as a Gold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A gold mask over Darrow's face, the false public face he is made to wear.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the recruitment and the surgery.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask reads as a disguise, a pretended face, which is the literal meaning of being carved to pass.

storyboard.claim: Darrow enters the Institute as an infiltrator.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow walks across the stone arena of the Institute, a determined step among Gold students.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mask of 212 now walks into the Gold school.
storyboard.addedInformation: The arena setting names the place; the walk reads as entering it.

storyboard.claim: Darrow sits in the opulent draft room among the Gold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow seated on a gilded bench in the marble draft room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the infiltrator in the Gold setting.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gold hall shows the opulence; the seated Red shows he does not belong.

callout.text: An Ivy League mixer on steroids

storyboard.claim: The Gold drinking and gossip feels like an Ivy League mixer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus and Julian in togas chat over wine glasses in the gold hall.
storyboard.onScreenText: An Ivy League mixer on steroids
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the civilised surface before the floor drops out.
storyboard.addedInformation: Togas and wine show the civilised gloss; the callout gives the narrator's own comparison.

storyboard.claim: The civilised gathering ends in a sudden drop into the passage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow tipped off balance, airborne with motion streaks, afraid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mixer from 215 breaks into the passage ritual.
storyboard.addedInformation: Falling reads as a sudden drop, matching the callout.

storyboard.claim: Darrow is stripped, drugged and locked in a freezing stone room with Julian.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tiny stone room; Darrow afraid, Julian beside him, the door sealed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The drop from 216 lands in a stone cell.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two different builds (Darrow lean, Julian slight pale) keep the pair distinct.

storyboard.claim: Julian is one of the few Golds who is kind and gentle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julian with a warm, gentle smile turned toward Darrow in the stone room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the cell into a human encounter.
storyboard.addedInformation: Happy here is genuine warmth, the one Gold who is not a threat.

storyboard.claim: They are friends, but the rules of the passage control the room.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julian and Darrow looking up at an unseen speaker that controls them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The friendship from 218 is overruled by the passage.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puppeteer reads as one party controlling others, which is what the broadcast does.

storyboard.claim: Only one can unlock the door; they must beat each other with bare hands.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow strikes toward Julian, who fights back, in the stone room with a door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The rule from 219 forces violence between friends.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fighting is drawn with two cast members, so it reads as a fight.

storyboard.claim: The rulers' children must survive an intimate murder before education begins.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus in the gold hall, thoughtful and strained, remembering the passage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Widens the passage from one pair to the whole Gold class.
storyboard.addedInformation: Worried plus think reads strain, not a happy memory.

storyboard.claim: The older generation deliberately traumatises its own children.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus points at an unseen younger Gold in the hall with a hard, angry face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The adults who designed the passage.
storyboard.addedInformation: The narration is cut off after their own; children is taken from the sentence's sense and is the only fit.

storyboard.claim: The ruling class must never weaken its grip.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus speaks directly out with a hard face, addressing the viewer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why 222 happens.
storyboard.addedInformation: Talk with an angry face reads as a warning, not a smile.

storyboard.claim: The passage is a beta test of human empathy: a stress test that decides who rules.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three-step chain: manufactured nightmare -> empathy tested -> graduate to rule.
storyboard.onScreenText: Manufactured nightmare -> Empathy tested -> Graduate to rule
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The beta-test idea from 223 made into a sequence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the causal order the narrator implies: test first, rule after.

storyboard.claim: If empathy breaks a child in the test, the child dies; if not, the child rules.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus, cold and unmoved, in the gold hall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the chain from 224.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cold face shows indifference to the outcome.

storyboard.claim: Mickey, the carver, alters Darrow's body and explains the quality board.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow on the carving table, body being altered; Mickey is not drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the passage to the surgery that made Darrow a Gold.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: Mickey is not drawn; the carved body and the name in the callout carry him.

storyboard.claim: The Board of Quality Control runs the Gold birth system with ruthless logic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus explains with a hard, sharp face in the gold hall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the board that governs Gold births.
storyboard.addedInformation: Angry talk reads as a system being defended, not a friendly host.

storyboard.claim: The state uses catalysts on lower-colour pregnancies to speed up gestation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Eo, a Red woman, with a worried face in a dim mine room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves to the Red side of the same policy.
storyboard.addedInformation: No medical icon: medical reads as healthcare, which would mislead.

storyboard.claim: Red births are sped up for the workforce; Gold births take the full nine months.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two buckets: Red born fast, Gold nine months.
storyboard.onScreenText: Red: born fast | Gold: nine months
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the Red policy from 228 with the Gold policy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sorter makes the two policies a visible split.

storyboard.claim: Gold births are forbidden medical help, making birth dangerous on purpose.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Eo, afraid, facing the viewer in the dim room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the sorter from 229.
storyboard.addedInformation: Afraid reads the danger the callout asks about.

storyboard.claim: The Board wants nature to kill the weak as a eugenic policy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus points with a fanatical, hard face in the gold hall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why no medical help is allowed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Angry point reads fanatical conviction.

storyboard.claim: The Board's quota is 13.6% of Gold children dying before their first birthday.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave icon: the quota is a death count.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The quota that the policy of 231 serves.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grave reads death literally, which is the claim.

storyboard.claim: When nature misses the quota, the Board kills Gold infants to make the number fit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus, blank and unmoved, in the gold hall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The quota from 232 enforced by the Board.
storyboard.addedInformation: Blank reads indifference, the apathy the act needs.

storyboard.claim: The Golds may seem victims of the system; the narrator asks whether that is so.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance weighing two sides: the Golds as victims against the Board.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A question raised by 233.
storyboard.addedInformation: Balance reads weighing two sides, the fairness question being asked.

storyboard.claim: The Golds seem as trapped by the Board as the Reds are by the mines.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains: the bound state the comparison names.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question of 234 with a comparison.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains read bound and imprisoned, the literal trap the narration describes.

storyboard.claim: The narrator rejects the idea that the Golds are victims.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator speaks directly; the words on screen say the Golds are not victims but beneficiaries.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the trap idea from 235.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the rejected phrase; no face is needed for a rejection.

callout.text: Buy the right to be remorseless

storyboard.claim: The Golds use their trauma to buy the moral right to be remorseless.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Titus, blank and unmoved, in the gold hall.
storyboard.onScreenText: Buy the right to be remorseless
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the beneficiary idea from 236.
storyboard.addedInformation: Blank reads the remorseless apathy the callout names.

storyboard.claim: Julian was chosen for the room because he was kind and had no ambition.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julian, sad, in the stone room with Darrow; a target marks him as chosen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to Julian from the passage.
storyboard.addedInformation: Target reads being chosen, the sense of who was picked.

storyboard.claim: The Board treats Julian as dead weight and disposes of him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julian collapsed on the floor, eyes shut, dead.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The consequence of 238: Julian is dead.
storyboard.addedInformation: Collapsed reads fallen and dead on the floor.
